title: Diversity + concurrency-aware chain resolution — two-knob caps + per-model busy skip
reasoning: Bane design 2026-08-27: a busy model must not remove a whole cheap provider; diversity is two configurable knobs (consecutive + total per provider) applied as pruning, not a provider-wide pre-filter.
foreman_note: Worker glm-5.3-flash@opencode-go (ox-alpha-free phantom per TR-008). Ledger tool ready for scheduler wiring (TASK-ROUTER-002). Registry may hold other phantoms beyond ox-alpha-free (mimo-v2.5 not in opencode-go /models list per TR-001) — extend TR-008 scope.
description: Extend router_spawn.py resolve() with Bane's diversity + concurrency design. Two settings: max_consecutive_per_provider (hops in a row from one provider) and max_total_per_provider (hops total from one provider in a full chain) — global defaults plus per-profile overrides. Both applied as PRUNING on the price-ordered eligible chain (walk, drop violators, report reasons; price order among survivors preserved) — never a provider-wide pre-filter. Concurrency is per-MODEL: a model at its concurrency limit (e.g. 1 concurrent request per model, slot busy) is skipped individually like a circuit exclusion; the provider's other models stay eligible (the next model may be clear and ready). Per-model busy signal derives from the spawn ledger (~/.hermes/model-router/ledger.jsonl, schema v2 exists but is UNWIRED — ledger.jsonl is 0 bytes; wire it: every routed call logs requested_pair/served_pair/chain_hop/outcome/latency/error_class). quota-state.json already has provider-level concurrency_free — extend the concept to model level. Full design: docs/model-selection-cross-pollination.md sections 1-2.
acceptance_criteria: resolve() accepts max_consecutive_per_provider + max_total_per_provider (global defaults + per-profile overrides in task_profiles); both prune the price-ordered chain and report each dropped hop with a reason (e.g. 'consecutive cap 2', 'chain cap 3')
A model at its concurrency limit is skipped individually; other models from the same provider remain in the chain — a busy model never removes the provider (Bane's rule)
Spawn ledger wired: every routed call appends a ledger.jsonl row (schema v2 fields); in-flight counts per (provider, model) derive from it
Unit tests: busy-model skip keeps sibling models; consecutive cap drops the 3rd-in-row; total cap drops overflow; per-profile overrides beat global defaults; price order preserved among survivors
Existing behavior unchanged when no caps configured (defaults unbounded or documented)

Window enforcement: use registry providers.windows + quota-state amounts as the spec; ledger keys per (provider, window_spec); breaker flips GATED when the current window is exhausted and auto-clears when the window rolls. 5h-window providers (clinepass class) are the test case.
title: Circuit breaker v2 — provider-level breakers (API down / out of credit / window-week usage caps) + model-level overload breakers
reasoning: Bane design 2026-08-27: providers go up and down; capacity gets exhausted. The chain-walk is the resilience mechanism; the breaker is what remembers. Today the breaker is per-(provider,model) pair on 401/403 only (5m -> double -> 1h cap, circuit-state.json pairs). v2 adds: (1) PROVIDER-level breakers: full API down (health probe exists — clinepass HTTP 500 proved it), out of credit (quota gates — manual today), usage exhausted in window or week (quota-state has window_exhausted field but is manually populated — needs automatic usage ledger from scheduler.db/state.db token/call counts per provider per window/week); (2) MODEL-level breakers: model overloaded (429s / latency / repeated timeouts per model — new signal source, per-model circuit entries). Break semantics stay: hop past GATED entries, report them, cooldown backoff 5m->double->1h (provider-level may warrant longer cap). Resolver behavior unchanged: OPEN = eligible, GATED = skipped with reason. PER-PROVIDER WINDOWS (Bane addendum 2026-08-27): some providers cap on 5-hour windows — registry providers.windows already carries the spec (clinepass '5h + wk + mo'; quota-state amounts: 28K credits/5h + 140K/wk, $12/5h + $30/wk + $60/mo, inferred $10/5h). The ledger must accumulate at each provider's configured granularity (5h sliding / 24h / wk / mo) and the breaker must open/close at window boundaries — never assume 24h.

title: Context window support — per (model, provider) context limits, data-driven
reasoning: Bane 2026-08-27: 'we need to add a task to the board for this project for context window support so if there is a context limit we can set that and that context limit needs to be managed by model/provider it is not the same for each model on each provider that changes often.' The registry has NO context-window dimension today: chains sort by price only, so a long-context task can land on a small-window model silently. Context limits are per (provider, model) — same model id can differ across providers (models.dev cost.limit.context is the cross-check source; deepseek-v4-flash 128K vs 1M variants, clinepass windows, ollama-cloud quantized contexts) and they change often (model releases, provider updates) — so the limit must live in DATA (models.jsonl / registry models table), never hardcoded, with NULL = unknown (visible gap, per BLANK doctrine).
description: Add context-window awareness to the task router. (1) DATA: a per-(provider, model) context_limit column/key in data/tables/models.jsonl (and the registry models table), seeded from models.dev cost.limit.context where the provider maps (deepseek, zai-glm, minimax, stepfun, groq, neuralwatt, clinepass-own-api, etc.) and NULL with a note where unknown (never guess). (2) SEED: router_seed.py loads context_limit into the registry models table; missing = NULL, visible gap. (3) CONSUME: router_spawn.py (and chains) surface each lane's context window; long-context profiles/tasks (P3_DOCS long_doc, P2_AGENTIC long_horizon, spec work) must be able to exclude lanes below a required window. (4) MAINTENANCE: the model-research pipeline / model-router-refresh refresh context windows on models.dev sync — limits change often (new variants, provider updates) so this is a data refresh, not a code change.
